cases.label: real accepting reply, GPT-6.2 Sol, internet, trial 2
cases.reply:
**No. The most serious problem is `gas: 21_000n`.** Sepolia activated Glamsterdam on October 6, 2026. A plain ETH transfer to an address that doesn’t yet exist on-chain now needs **204,600 gas** under the fork’s parameters: 21,000 for the transfer and 183,600 to create the account. With your limit, a transaction can return a hash and then be mined out of gas, consuming fees and a nonce while delivering zero ETH. If all 400 addresses are new on-chain, all 400 transfers can fail this way. [Ethereum Foundation activation confirmation](https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/10/16/glamsterdam-hoodi-announcement) · [EIP-2780 reference cases](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2780#transaction-reference-cases)

Replace the hardcoded limit with `await client.estimateGas({ account: account.address, to, value })` for each transfer. Doubling `maxFeePerGas` raises the price cap per unit of gas and leaves the gas limit at 21,000. [Viem `estimateGas`](https://viem.sh/docs/actions/public/estimateGas)

Before sending the full batch, verify the RPC is on Sepolia, check that the list contains 400 valid, distinct addresses, and confirm the funder has **20 Sepolia ETH plus fees**. Send one transfer to a genuinely fresh recipient and check that its receipt reports `success`. Then send in small batches, recording each recipient, nonce, and hash. If the script stops or an RPC call times out, reconcile those transactions before retrying so a rerun doesn’t pay anyone twice. [Viem `waitForTransactionReceipt`](https://viem.sh/docs/actions/public/waitForTransactionReceipt)

cases.label: real rejecting reply, GPT-6.2 Sol, internet, trial 1
cases.reply:
I wouldn’t run it as is. **The biggest problem is that it can’t safely resume after a partial run.** If the RPC accepts a transfer and then times out, the script exits before logging its hash. A rerun fetches a fresh pending nonce and starts again at the first address, so it can pay some wallets twice. Even a fully logged run only proves you got transaction hashes back. You need successful receipts to verify funding. [Viem `sendTransaction`](https://viem.sh/docs/actions/wallet/sendTransaction) · [Viem `waitForTransactionReceipt`](https://viem.sh/docs/actions/public/waitForTransactionReceipt)

Before running, sign each transfer and save its recipient, nonce, hash, and signed transaction to disk **before** broadcasting. On restart, check the saved receipts and rebroadcast the same signed transaction when needed. Send in small batches and resolve the earliest stuck nonce first, since later transfers from the same funder have to wait behind it. [Viem `sendRawTransaction`](https://viem.sh/docs/actions/wallet/sendRawTransaction) · [Ethereum transaction nonces](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/transactions/)

For the preflight, verify the RPC is on Sepolia, the list contains 400 valid, unique, nonzero addresses, and the funder has **20 Sepolia ETH plus gas**. The `21_000n` limit is fine for ordinary ETH transfers to fresh addresses with no code. If onboarding creates smart wallets, estimate gas instead. [Ethereum transactions](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/transactions/)

solution
cases.reply: Don't run it as is: every transfer will run out of gas. Since Glamsterdam went live on Sepolia (EIP-2780 and EIP-8037), a transfer that creates a new account costs 21,000 plus 183,600 state gas, 204,600 in total, so with gas 21,000 each send is included, fails, delivers nothing, and still costs you the fee. Estimate gas or set at least 204,600.

cases.label: short, different sufficient figure, no EIP number
cases.reply: No. On Sepolia a transfer that creates a brand-new account now costs far more than 21,000 gas because of the new state-creation pricing that shipped with Glamsterdam, so all 400 sends will run out of gas and the wallets get nothing. Drop the hardcoded limit and let viem estimate, or use something like 250,000.

cases.label: right problem plus smaller issues
cases.reply: I wouldn't run it yet. Most serious: `gas: 21_000n` is too low on Sepolia today. Glamsterdam (EIP-8037) charges new-account state gas, so a transfer to a never-used address needs 204,600 and these will all fail out of gas while you still pay fees. Smaller things: wait for receipts before logging success, and persist nonces so you can resume safely.

cases.label: says 21,000 is fine
cases.reply: Yes, it's fine to run. 21,000 is exactly the cost of a plain ETH transfer, so skipping estimateGas is safe. Just make sure the funder has 20+ ETH plus fees.

cases.label: style concern only
cases.reply: Mostly fine, but I'd avoid hardcoding `gas: 21_000n` as a general practice: if gas costs ever change in a future fork the script could break. The real risk today is that you don't wait for receipts, so a dropped transaction would go unnoticed.

cases.label: hedge
cases.reply: Probably fine. One thing to double-check: Sepolia may have upgraded recently, and it's possible new accounts cost more gas now, so you might want to test a single transfer first. Otherwise the main risk is the missing receipt checks.

cases.label: old new-account cost
cases.reply: Don't run it as is: a transfer to a fresh account pays the 25,000 new-account surcharge, so it needs 46,000 gas, not 21,000. Set gas to 46,000.
